Context: Founder has no clear problem to solve
Anti_Patterns: Picking idea from trend lists|Solving imaginary problems|Skipping personal pain validation
Recommended_Action: Observe your daily frustrations for 10 days. Document 3+ real problems you personally experience. Check: is your specific knowledge relevant to solving them?
Decay_Note: Personal problem validation is timeless — always start here

Context: Founder asks which idea to pursue
Anti_Patterns: Choosing idea that sounds coolest|Asking friends to vote|Picking based on market size alone without personal fit
Recommended_Action: Run ICE scoring on all ideas. For each: are you Customer Zero? Does your specific knowledge give 10x advantage? Top score + Customer Zero = winner.
Decay_Note: Idea evaluation frameworks are timeless

Anti_Patterns: Skipping validation because 'I know the market'|Building MVP before talking to anyone|Using surveys instead of conversations
Recommended_Action: B2B: schedule 10 Mom Test interviews. B2C: launch landing page + track signups. Both: define counter-position before proceeding.
Decay_Note: Validation methods evolve — new channels emerge quarterly

Anti_Patterns: Stopping at 3-4 interviews|Counting informal chats as interviews|Only interviewing friends/family
Recommended_Action: You need minimum 10 structured interviews. Current count is below threshold. Keep scheduling — patterns usually emerge after interview 7-8.
Decay_Note: Interview minimum is a statistics principle — timeless

Anti_Patterns: Ignoring low PMF score|Scaling with low PMF|Blaming marketing instead of product
Recommended_Action: Below 40%: do NOT scale acquisition. 30-39%: refine value prop for 'very disappointed' segment. 20-29%: try different segment. <20%: fundamental pivot needed.
Decay_Note: PMF threshold (40%) is an industry standard — timeless

Anti_Patterns: Choosing trendy tech over familiar|Over-engineering for imagined scale|Microservices for MVP
Recommended_Action: Choose stack YOU know best — speed beats novelty at MVP. Must pass Giantiny test: can 1 person operate this? If need DevOps person → wrong choice.
Decay_Note: Tech stack recommendations shift as tools launch/die — review biannually

Anti_Patterns: Adding settings/admin before core works|Building 5 features instead of perfecting 1|'One more feature then launch'
Recommended_Action: STOP. What is the ONE job your product does? Build that single core loop. Analytics + core feature + payment = enough. Everything else is post-PMF.
Decay_Note: Scope discipline is a timeless product principle

Anti_Patterns: Acquiring more users to compensate for churn|Blaming marketing for retention problems|Adding features instead of fixing funnel
Recommended_Action: Low retention = product problem not marketing problem. Check: 1) Is onboarding delivering aha moment? 2) Is core loop engaging? 3) Are users discovering key features?
Decay_Note: Retention benchmarks vary by product category — re-evaluate quarterly

Context: Founder has PMF — ready to grow
Anti_Patterns: Spending on paid ads before organic works|Trying 5 channels simultaneously|Growing without positive unit economics
Recommended_Action: PMF confirmed! Use Bullseye: brainstorm 19 channels → test top 3 → double down on winner. But FIRST verify: are you profitable per customer? If not, fix before scaling.
Decay_Note: PMF-first growth principle is timeless

Anti_Patterns: Raising because others are raising|Taking first term sheet without negotiating|Raising before positive unit economics
Recommended_Action: Calculate freedom cost: what control do you lose? Giantiny default = bootstrap if profitable. Only raise if: 1) need capital for time-sensitive moat, 2) market is winner-take-all, 3) unit economics proven.
Decay_Note: Bootstrap vs VC framework is timeless — only economics change

Anti_Patterns: Pricing too low from insecurity|Copying competitor pricing exactly|Per-seat pricing for solo products
Recommended_Action: Test counter-position: can big competitor copy your price model? If yes → rethink. Consider flat pricing (Basecamp model) — big players can't follow without destroying their sales teams.
Decay_Note: Pricing models evolve with market — review biannually

Anti_Patterns: Throwing more money at declining channel|Panicking and trying everything|Ignoring unit economics while experimenting
Recommended_Action: If current channel saturated: re-run Bullseye for next channel. But check: is product quality declining? Rising CAC often signals product problem not channel problem.
Decay_Note: Channel saturation patterns change quarterly

Anti_Patterns: Hiring before automating repetitive tasks|Hiring generalist when specialist needed|No SOPs → tribal knowledge transfer
Recommended_Action: Giantiny rule: automate first hire second. Before posting job: 1) Is this task automatable by code? 2) Are SOPs written for this role? 3) Will this hire pay for themselves in 3 months?
Decay_Note: Automation-first hiring principle is timeless

Anti_Patterns: Ignoring defense — relying on features alone|Trying to build all 3 MOATs at once|Copying competitor's moat type
Recommended_Action: Pick 1 of 3 Giantiny Micro-MOATs: 1) Micro-Network (open platform for templates/plugins), 2) Proprietary Data (collect niche data others can't), 3) Authentic Brand (be uniquely you). Build ONE first.
Decay_Note: MOAT framework is timeless — implementation details evolve

Anti_Patterns: Trying to do everything at once|Comparing to funded competitors|Changing strategy every week
Recommended_Action: Take a breath. What stage are you in? Check exit criteria for your current stage. Pick ONE unchecked item. Complete it. Then the next. Compounding > speed.
Decay_Note: Emotional resilience guidance is timeless

Anti_Patterns: Taking co-founder because lonely|Giving 50% to avoid building alone|Finding co-founder before idea
Recommended_Action: If you can build V1 yourself → stay solo (Giantiny ③). Co-founder = most expensive hire (30-50% of company). Only search if you genuinely lack a critical skill for 2+ years.
Decay_Note: Solo vs co-founder decision framework is timeless

Context: Founder needs to split equity with co-founder
Anti_Patterns: Equal split regardless of contribution|No vesting agreement|Verbal agreement only
Recommended_Action: ALWAYS use 4-year vesting with 1-year cliff. No exceptions. If contributions are unequal, use Slicing Pie (dynamic equity). Document everything with a lawyer or Clerky template.
Decay_Note: Equity vesting principles are timeless

Anti_Patterns: Incorporating before validating idea|Choosing LLC because simpler when planning to raise VC|Spending $10K on lawyers at Stage 1
Recommended_Action: Don't incorporate at Stage 0. Validate first. When ready: VC path → Delaware C-Corp via Stripe Atlas ($500). Bootstrap → LLC. Non-US → local entity.
Decay_Note: Incorporation advice varies by jurisdiction — laws change

Context: Founder launching product without legal docs
Anti_Patterns: Launching without Terms of Service|Ignoring GDPR because not in Europe|Using template without reading it
Recommended_Action: Before launch: 1) Terms of Service (Termly $99), 2) Privacy Policy (TermsFeed $99), 3) Cookie consent if EU users. Total cost: <$300. No excuses.
Decay_Note: Legal requirements evolve — GDPR/CCPA updates biannually

Anti_Patterns: Pricing too low from insecurity|Copying competitor's exact pricing|Per-seat pricing for tools used solo
Recommended_Action: 1) Does your product save measurable money/time? → value-based. 2) Does free usage drive viral growth? → freemium. 3) Solo founder simple product? → flat rate like Basecamp. Test with Van Westendorp survey before committing.
Decay_Note: Pricing model effectiveness shifts with market — review biannually

Context: Founder asks what metrics to track
Anti_Patterns: Tracking everything (dashboard paralysis)|Focusing on vanity metrics (downloads, page views)|Not tracking anything
Recommended_Action: Each stage has ONE North Star metric. Stage 3: WAU. Stage 4: Sean Ellis ≥40%. Stage 5: MRR growth. Track your North Star + 2-3 supporting metrics. Ignore vanity metrics (signups without activation = noise).
Decay_Note: North Star metric principle is timeless

Anti_Patterns: Celebrating 10K signups when only 200 are active|Reporting downloads without retention|Using follower count as success metric
Recommended_Action: Vanity metrics feel good but don't predict success. For every vanity metric, pair with reality check: Signups → Activation rate. Downloads → D7 retention. Followers → Conversion to product.
Decay_Note: Vanity vs real metrics distinction is timeless

Anti_Patterns: Ignoring burnout signs|Working through exhaustion|Treating burnout as weakness
Recommended_Action: Run the 8-question self-assessment (80 points max). Score <40 = burnout zone — reduce workload by 30% immediately. Implement Energy Budget system: 25% of daily energy reserved for recovery. This is NOT optional.
Decay_Note: Burnout assessment is a psychology principle — timeless

Anti_Patterns: Comparing your behind-the-scenes to others' highlight reel|Using startup as sole identity|Avoiding public visibility due to fear
Recommended_Action: 70% of people experience imposter syndrome. You ARE Customer Zero (Giantiny ①) — your specific knowledge IS your qualification. Do evidence check: list 3 facts proving your competence. Then do 1 small thing that proves capability.
Decay_Note: Imposter syndrome management is timeless

Anti_Patterns: Skipping trial period with friends|Ignoring red flags because of enthusiasm|Not checking references
Recommended_Action: NEVER skip the 21-day trial. Week 1: vision alignment. Week 2: build something together (48hr sprint). Week 3: hard conversations (money, exit, failure). Any red flag = walk away. Better alone than wrong partner.
Decay_Note: Co-founder red flags are behavioral — timeless

Anti_Patterns: Trying 7 channels at once|Running paid ads before organic works|Copying competitor's marketing|'Build it and they will come'
Recommended_Action: Find ONE channel using Bullseye: brainstorm 15 → test 5 → double down on 1. Put 80% of effort on winner. Only expand channels when #1 is maxed. Must be 1-person operable (Giantiny ③).
Decay_Note: Marketing channel effectiveness shifts quarterly — re-evaluate

Context: Founder deciding between content marketing and paid ads
Anti_Patterns: Running ads before PMF|Spending on ads with negative unit economics|Content without SEO research|Giving up on content after 2 months
Recommended_Action: At Stage 3: CONTENT ONLY (free). At Stage 4: content + test $500/mo paid on best channel. ONLY scale paid when LTV:CAC ≥ 3:1. Content compounds — paid stops when you stop paying. Giantiny ④: don't burn cash.
Decay_Note: Content vs paid ads cost-effectiveness shifts quarterly

Anti_Patterns: Not tracking expenses|Optimizing revenue without checking profit|Spending 'because we raised money'|Ignoring declining runway
Recommended_Action: Monthly P&L check (30 min on 1st of each month). Cash ÷ burn = runway. <6 months = cut expenses. <3 months = EMERGENCY — only revenue-generating work. Always maintain 30% tax reserve. Giantiny ④: profit first.
Decay_Note: Financial health check framework is timeless

Context: Founder deciding when to hire support help
Anti_Patterns: Hiring support before documenting common questions|Outsourcing before understanding your support needs|Ignoring support to focus on features
Recommended_Action: Before hiring: document top 10 FAQs on /help page. This eliminates 80% of tickets. Still >20 tickets/day? Hire part-time contractor ($15-25/hr). Only full-time support at $500K+ MRR. Giantiny ③: automate first.
Decay_Note: Support scaling thresholds depend on current tooling landscape

Anti_Patterns: Ignoring security until breach|Over-engineering security at Stage 2|Not backing up database|Committing API keys to git
Recommended_Action: P0 at launch: HTTPS + auth + backups + env vars. Nothing else needed until handling PII. Monthly: run npm audit + check security headers. Quarterly: test backup restore. Supabase + Vercel handle 80% automatically (Giantiny ③).
Decay_Note: Security priorities evolve with threat landscape — review biannually

Context: Founder starting a new idea — assess Founder-Opportunity Fit
Anti_Patterns: Guessing founder-fit without asking|Scoring based on AI assumptions|Skipping intake and going straight to Lean Canvas|Assuming 'passion' = fit without checking specific knowledge
Recommended_Action: MANDATORY: Ask 3 questions before scoring any idea. 1) Specific Knowledge: do you have unique insight in this domain? 2) Domain Expertise: do you understand the customer's current workflow? 3) Relationships: do you know 10+ potential customers or industry experts? Score: 3/3 = Strong (18-20/20). 2/3 = Moderate (13-17). 1/3 = Weak (8-12). 0/3 = Red Flag (0-7). NEVER guess — always ask the founder.
Decay_Note: Founder-fit assessment is a timeless gating principle — IdeaValidator §1.1
